N13.root_cause: returns were generated only for live slots; when the cross-section shrinks, stocks leave `alive` and their next-month returns are NaN, so any 3-month response spanning a shrink month is NaN and the whole slope series becomes NaN

N7.note: systematic variance exceeds the fixed total, so the idiosyncratic sd hit the 1e-6 floor (0.1% a month instead of about 5%); the world was nearly noise-free

A_defects.classifier: the v1 driver applied only the adequacy part of protocol 6.1 (four worlds) and not 'any failed or incomplete scenario -> D'; v2 computes the classification with one function tested against the written rule

D_quiet_market.explanation: v1 slope noise was essentially cross-sectional sampling noise (order 1/sqrt(N); the v1 'implied' figure divides by the TOTAL return sd, so it sits slightly below that scale). Control-factor shocks would add about 0.045 to a univariate IC through the signal's 0.05-0.18 correlations, but the multivariate FM absorbs them in the control coefficients; sector shocks are absorbed by the sector dummies. v1 had NO time-varying payoff on the signal itself, which is what makes a real IC vary month to month (LH-CP4's 0.06-0.12 range). The quiet market is therefore a missing DGP component, not an SE scaling problem: cross-sectional dispersion (6.5%/month) was realistic, IC dispersion and its serial correlation were not (no signal payoff), premium variability existed only in N6 / N9, and residual noise was realistic except in N7 (defect)

kind: OC-2 v2 failure-mode audit (v1 code reproduction + population algebra; no returns simulated)
